Shipped definitions: carriers and the IPCC 2006 fuel defaults

Source: R/shipped-scales.R
shipped_scales.Rd

nestedscales ships one scale definition, carriers, under inst/scales/, and the IPCC tables it draws on under inst/extdata/. read_scale("carriers") reads the scale; scale_catalog() lists it with every other registered definition.

Source

energypal carriers.yml; IPCC (2006), 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories, Volume 2 (Energy), Chapter 1, Tables 1.2 and 1.4, https://www.ipcc-nggip.iges.or.jp/public/2006gl/. Transcribed in data-raw/ipcc2006/.

carriers

A scale of 71 fuels in three nested frames, group (8) > carrier (17) > fuel (71), key fuel, taken from the carriers palette of the energypal package (its inst/extdata/palettes/carriers.yml, which cites the IPCC 2006 Guidelines and the IEA World Energy Balances for its classification). energypal remains the editable source of the names, hierarchy, labels and aliases; the definition is a snapshot built by data-raw/carriers.R, which stops when the two disagree.

The three carriers energypal declares without subtypes (Electricity, Heat, Other) become their own fuel, so every carrier is reachable from the atoms. Five names appear both as a group and as the carrier inside it (Nuclear, Electricity, Heat, Storage, Other), and Hydrogen is both a carrier (under Synthetic) and a fuel (under Storage): every lookup names its frame.

Attributes (source "IPCC2006", 26 rows): the default net calorific value lhv (kind property, GJ/t) and CO2 emission factor ef_co2 (kind factor, kg/TJ) of the IPCC 2006 Guidelines, Vol. 2 Ch. 1, Tables 1.2 and 1.4, attached to the 13 fuels whose definition matches an IPCC fuel exactly. Fuels without a matching IPCC entry carry no value; scale_attributes() reports them as NA rather than inventing one.

Aliases (136 rows): energypal's alternative spellings (source "energypal") and a set of model commodity codes such as GAS, LIG, ELC (source "commodity"). scale_match() resolves them.

meta$labels carries energypal's short and long labels per member; meta$energypal_version and meta$palette_version record the snapshot. Colours are not stored: join them from energypal by name.

IPCC 2006 default calorific values and CO2 emission factors

system.file("extdata", "ipcc2006_fuel_defaults.csv", package = "nestedscales") holds every row of Table 1.2 (default net calorific values, TJ/Gg, with the lower and upper limits of the 95% confidence interval) and Table 1.4 (default CO2 emission factors for combustion, kg/TJ, with the 95% interval) of the IPCC 2006 Guidelines, Vol. 2 (Energy), Chapter 1, in long form, together with how each IPCC fuel maps onto carriers. TJ/Gg is numerically identical to GJ/t, the unit the lhv attribute uses. One row per IPCC fuel and attribute:

ipcc_fuel

The fuel's English description in the Guidelines.

attribute

"lhv" (Table 1.2) or "ef_co2" (Table 1.4).

kind

"property" or "factor", see SCALE_ATTRIBUTE_KINDS.

value, lower, upper

The default and its 95% interval.

unit_of_measure

"GJ/t" or "kg/TJ".

table

"1.2" or "1.4".

source

"IPCC2006".

frame, unit

The carriers member the row maps to (NA when not mapped).

mapping_status

"mapped" (an exact or definitional correspondence), "review" (a plausible correspondence awaiting a ruling; not attached) or "unmapped" (no counterpart).

primary

Whether this IPCC fuel is the one carriers carries for that member. Only mapped rows with primary = TRUE enter the scale's attributes.

See also

read_scale(), scale_catalog(), convert_scale(); vignette("attributes").

Examples

carriers <- read_scale("carriers")
carriers
#> NestedScale: carriers
#> Description: Energy carriers: fuels and energy vectors with subtypes, from energypal's carriers palette (IPCC 2006 / IEA classifications) 
#> Frames (3, coarsest first):
#>   - group (8)
#>     - carrier (17)
#>       - fuel (71)
#> Atoms: 71
#> Attributes: lhv, ef_co2 (sources: IPCC2006) -- 26 at fuel
#> Aliases: 136 (energypal, commodity)
#> Source: energypal carriers.yml
scale_units(carriers, "carrier")
#>  [1] "FossilCoal"          "FossilOil"           "FossilGas"          
#>  [4] "Bioenergy"           "Hydro"               "Wind"               
#>  [7] "Solar"               "Geothermal"          "OtherRenewables"    
#> [10] "Nuclear"             "Electricity"         "Heat"               
#> [13] "Hydrogen"            "HydrogenDerivatives" "SyntheticFuels"     
#> [16] "Storage"             "Other"              
scale_attributes(carriers, "lhv", frame = "fuel")
